# bugs #3973: Pointers to void and integers that are initialized with a string literal get bytes of a host address

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3973/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17192
- Recommended action: Apply after the patch for local 0001. Confirm error 2 for bit-fields and floats and the tag byte on mcs51, then close.
- Patch: [bugs-3973.patch](../../patches/bugs-3973.patch), commit [`5014cb0c9`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/5014cb0c9e50fd62eedec3235fa680def68d21c4). Apply after `local-0001.patch`.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

In the test case of the ticket, the `const char *` member gets the label of the string, and the
`const void *` and `uint32_t` members get literal bytes. With `sdcc -mmcs51 -c` on r17176 they
were `40 11 62` and `40 11 62 4a` in one run and `40 91 a1` and `40 91 a1 f1` in the next. The
bytes are the low bytes of the compiler's own pointer to the characters. In a run under gdb the
pointer was `0x55a9d50d9fe0`, and the compiler wrote `e0 9f 0d` and `e0 9f 0d d5`. The author of
the second comment reads the bytes as the characters, which would be `41 41 41`.

Two patches of this report correct the two members. The patch for local 0001 corrects the
`const void *` member. On r17192 with the patches of this report up to that one, the `uint32_t`
member got `f0 40 16 12` in one run, and this patch corrects it.

On mcs51, stm8, and z80, integers of 1, 2, 4, and 8 bytes that are initialized by data with a
cast of a string literal get such bytes as objects, as array elements, and as struct members.
When only integers refer to a literal, the string is absent from the assembly. Bit-fields get
bits of the pointer, and `float` objects get it as their value.

## Cause

For a string literal, `constExprValue` in `src/SDCCast.c` returns a value that has the storage
class `S_LITERAL` and the label of the string as its name. The numeric members of its union
overlap `v_char`, the pointer to the characters. `list2val` in `src/SDCCval.c` removes the cast
and returns this value, and `printIvalType` and `printIvalBitFields` in `src/SDCCglue.c` print
its number. Only `printIvalCharPtr` adds strings to `ccpStr`, the set that `emitStaticSeg`
consults before it emits a string. The entry for local 0001 has the cause for the `const void *`
member.

## Fix

`printIvalType` recognizes the value by `IS_LITERAL` and by the `isstrlit` count of its symbol.
For integer types it prints the label of the string in the loop that prints the address of an
object, and it adds the string to `ccpStr` and the symbol to `statsg->syms`, as
`printIvalCharPtr` does. `_Bool` objects get 1, as they do without the patch. For `float` it
reports error 2, "Initializer element is not a constant expression". `printIvalBitFields`
reports error 2 for the value, as it does for the address of an object.

## Decision

- On mcs51 the byte above the two address bytes is `0x80`, the tag of a generic pointer to code
  memory. The `uint32_t` member gets `.db __str_0, (__str_0 >> 8), #0x80, #0x00`. The code that
  mcs51 generates for `(unsigned long)"AAA"` stores these four bytes, and the small model
  initializes objects in data memory with that code. In ucsim, integers of 1, 2, 4, and 8 bytes
  in data were equal to the value of the cast in code. The condition is `GPTRSIZE > FARPTRSIZE`,
  and stm8 and z80 get the address and zeros. The alternative is 0 in that byte, which the loop
  writes for `(unsigned long)&var`.
- Bit-fields and `float` objects that are initialized by data with a cast of a string literal get
  error 2. Without the patch these declarations compile without a diagnostic, and the data has
  bits of the compiler's pointer. gcc reports an error for both declarations.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3973.c` has the object of the ticket and integers to whose literals
only an integer refers. On r17192 with the patches of this report up to the one for local 0001,
it fails 19 of its 26 assertions on mcs51-small, mcs51-medium, and mcs51-small-stack-auto, 22 on
mcs51-large, mcs51-huge, and mcs51-large-stack-auto, 20 of 24 on stm8, and 19 of 24 on ucz80.
With the patch it passes on these eight targets and on host. On r17192 its assertion on the
`const void *` member fails too, so the test needs the patch for local 0001.
`support/valdiag/tests/bug-3973.c` expects an error for a bit-field and for a `float`, and
without the patch the compiler accepts both.

The patch does not change the assembly of the other regression tests for mcs51-small and
mcs51-large. With this patch and the patch for bug #4070 added to the earlier patches of this
report on r17192, the regression suite has 0 failures for host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and
ucz80, and the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80,
and stm8. The code size of every other test is equal with and without the two patches. ds390,
hc08, mos6502, pdk, and f8 were not built. pic14 has its own copies of the two functions in
`src/pic14/glue.c`, which the patch does not change.

## Related

- The entry for local 0001 lists pointer initializers with a string literal behind a cast, an
  offset, or `&`. The two patches do not correct them.
- For `(unsigned long)&var` with `var` in data memory, the data has 0 in the third byte with and
  without the patch, and the code that mcs51 generates stores the tag `0x40`. The data for
  `(unsigned long)&"QQQ"[1]` has 0 in that byte too, and its string is absent from the assembly.
- `constexpr unsigned long k = (unsigned long)"abc"; const unsigned long z = k + 1;` gets the
  host bytes plus 1 for `z` with the patch. The cause was not traced.
- Bug #3971 is a different defect. Feature request #892 concerns the upper byte of generic
  pointers in initializer data, and the patch that the first comment links belongs to it.
